text:
Alex R.: CI perf check failed on PR #7342 — microbench warmup + kernel selector thresholds. Blocker for rollout.
Alex R.: Perf job: ci/microbench/kernel_selector_warmup (linux/gpu) reported a 12.8% regression on kv_cache_hit_latency_p50 vs baseline.
Alex R.: pasted output:```FAILED: threshold_diff: +12.8% (p50)
baseline: 1.25ms
current: 1.41ms
metric: kv_cache_hit_latency_p50
commit: 9f3b2c1 -> 2a7d5ef (PR 7342)```
perf-bot: New perf alert: `ci/microbench/kernel_selector_warmup` - diff +12.8% (p50). See: https://perf.redwood-ci/reports/2051234567
Maria G.: ugh. PR touches kernel heuristic and the batching warmup path, right?
Alex R.: yeah small change in heuristic selection logic and a micro-optimization in kv cache warmup ordering. I didn't expect this to affect p50 that much.
Ryan H.: can you paste the microbench harness args and the exact seed? want to reproduce locally.
Alex R.: harness: `./run_microbench --bench kernel_selector_warmup --iters 1000 --seed 42 --target p50`
Alex R.: also running with `--kv-warmup=lazy` vs `--kv-warmup=eager` shows the gap disappears with eager.
Maria G.: interesting. maybe the change deferred some prefetch that used to hide kernel switch overhead.
Sanjay K.: can we bisect the change set in the PR? maybe one hunk caused the delta.
Ryan H.: doing a quick bisect on the PR branch locally, will ping with suspected commit.
perf-bot: Bisect helper: try `git bisect start --bad 2a7d5ef --good 9f3b2c1` and run `./tools/perf_ci_runner --bench kernel_selector_warmup`.
Ryan H.: bisect done. Culprit appears to be commit 2a12e7c — the `select_kernel_for_length()` fallback change.
Ryan H.: local perf compare: baseline p50 1.24ms -> with 2a12e7c p50 1.39ms (+12%). Full output:```compare: baseline=9f3b2c1 current=2a12e7c
kv_cache_hit_p50: 1.24ms -> 1.39ms (+12.1%)
batching_wait_p50: 0.44ms -> 0.46ms (+4.5%)
notes: increased kernel switch micro-overhead when sequence len ~ 96-128
```
Maria G.: good catch. That fallback change was meant to improve throughput for long sequences, but maybe it reduces fast-path for common mid-length cases.
Alex R.: should we revert the specific hunk and re-run CI? or add a conditional to keep the old fast-path for seq_len in [64,160]?
Sanjay K.: if rollout is blocked, revert is fastest. We can follow up with a targeted fix and perf tests covering mid-length distribution.
Maria G.: also add a microbench that includes the kv warmup variation (lazy/eager) so CI tests both modes. This will catch regressions like this.
Ryan H.: I'll open a revert PR for 2a12e7c now. Link in a sec.
Ryan H.: PR: #7346 Revert kernel fallback hunk (temp) — https://git.redwood/ryan/pr/7346 : will run full perf CI before merging.
Alex R.: thanks. also filing a follow-up issue to add microbench cases and an automated bisect job for kernel-selector diffs.
Maria G.: can we add a guard in the code to keep the previous fast-path active when `kv_cache.size()>0 && seq_len_between(64,160)`? quick patch might be safer than full revert.
Sanjay K.: true but quick patches can miss edge cases — revert + targeted patch after tests is lower risk for rollout.
Alex R.: agree. revert first. once CI green we iterate.
perf-bot: CI runs queued: perf CI for PR 7346 started. Current queue position: 2.
Maria G.: also pinging release for rollout hold: @release-team this blocks canary.
Alex R.: thanks all. I'll follow up with the perf regression issue and test matrix updates. :thumbsup:
